title: Designing Electro-Optical Chips
gist: As silicon photonics enters volume production for AI and data-center interconnect, the design flow is breaking: existing EDA infrastructure can be partly reused, but waveguides, optical phase, polarization and thermal drift demand specialized simulation, and DRC/LVS sign-off generates false errors on rasterized curves and same-layer waveguides. The unresolved gap is functional verification — photonic behavior is continuous physics, so today's practice is scripted sweeps (validation, not proof), which vendors from Cadence, Synopsys, Siemens EDA, Keysight and Axiomise all frame as the next five-year opportunity, likely closed with automation and agentic AI.

insights.claim: Silicon photonics is moving out of specialized research into mainstream semiconductor design because AI infrastructure, data centers and communications systems demand faster, lower-power optical interconnects.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Photonics demand is now tied to AI capex rather than niche telecom cycles, widening the addressable market for PIC foundries, EDA and optical-engine suppliers.
insights.quote: Silicon photonics is moving out of specialized research and into mainstream semiconductor design as AI infrastructure, data centers, and communications systems demand faster, lower-power optical interconnects.
insights.locator: Opening: 'Silicon photonics is moving out of specialized research'

insights.claim: Designing a photonic integrated circuit is only part of the challenge — engineers must confirm its performance inside an electro-optical-electrical (EOE) system, and traditional workflows separate those steps across PIC tools and system simulation platforms.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: The bottleneck is flow integration, not device physics — value accrues to vendors that own the stitched-together electro-optical flow rather than point photonic tools.
insights.quote: Engineers need to confirm its performance within an electro-optical-electrical (EOE) system.
insights.locator: 'As silicon photonics enters volume production'

insights.claim: Optical links in the network are migrating from pluggable modules to near-packaged optics and then to co-packaged optics, pushing optics physically closer to compute and multiplying the verification burden.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Each step toward co-packaged optics moves dollars from pluggable transceiver vendors to packaging, EDA and optical-engine suppliers embedded in the GPU/switch substrate.
insights.quote: The optics now is coming closer to compute, and you need a lot more verification in addition to just the photonic part.
insights.locator: Priyank Shukla, Synopsys — 'In the beginning, the photonic element'

insights.claim: Ayar Labs builds its optical engine as an electronics chip hybrid-bonded onto a photonic chip, which is then packaged onto a substrate alongside the GPU or switch, with the foundry doing the hybrid bonding and a downstream OSAT doing the substrate packaging.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Maps exactly where value is captured in co-packaged optics: foundry hybrid bonding, fabless optical-engine design, and OSAT substrate assembly are three separate P&Ls.
insights.quote: The optical engine architecture that we make is an electronics chip hybrid-bonded onto a photonic chip, and then that combination is packaged on a substrate alongside the GPU or the switch.
insights.locator: Vishal Chandrasekar, Ayar Labs

insights.claim: Much of the electro-optical design workflow is foundry-specific, so a design team's flow depends on which foundries it works with and the architecture it has chosen.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Foundry lock-in in photonics is stronger than in digital logic — switching costs protect incumbent PIC foundries and their PDK ecosystems.
insights.locator: Vishal Chandrasekar, Ayar Labs — 'Much of the workflow'

insights.claim: A practical optical-I/O system contains not only photonic devices but modulator drivers, transimpedance amplifiers, clocking circuits, monitoring photodiodes, heaters, control loops and calibration logic, so the photonic die, electronic die, package, laser, thermal system and fiber interface must be verified together.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Co-packaged optics is a systems-integration problem: suppliers who can only verify one domain will be squeezed out of the design win.
insights.quote: The photonic die, electronic die, package, laser, thermal system, and fiber interface must therefore be verified together.
insights.locator: John Bowers — 'Electronic-photonic co-design is especially important'

insights.claim: Because it is impractical to simulate an entire photonic circuit with a full-wave electromagnetic solver, each component is reduced to a compact model capturing loss, phase, wavelength response, reflection, modulation behavior and manufacturing variation, then assembled into a circuit-level simulation the way transistor models are in electronic design.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Compact-model quality is the choke point for photonic EDA adoption — whoever owns validated compact models owns the flow.
insights.quote: Because it is impractical to simulate an entire photonic circuit with a full-wave electromagnetic solver, each component is reduced to a compact model.
insights.locator: John Bowers — 'At the component level'

insights.claim: Photonic physical verification requires photonics-specific checks on top of familiar DRC and LVS, including optical-path continuity, bend-radius constraints, waveguide spacing, phase matching, insertion loss, reflections, thermal crosstalk, polarization behavior and wavelength alignment.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Each extra check class is a separate tool SKU — this list is effectively the product roadmap for photonic sign-off software.
insights.locator: John Bowers — 'Then, physical verification includes familiar electronic checks'

insights.claim: Photonic design teams typically work top-down from system requirements to circuit to component and then push updated models back up, because a component that misses its spec forces a return to the system level to re-trade the whole architecture.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Design iteration loops in photonics are architectural, not local — schedule risk in co-packaged optics programs is systematically underestimated.
insights.locator: Niels Fache, Keysight EDA — 'Design teams want to look at that as a system'

insights.claim: Photonic and electronic design share the same first-principles physics (Maxwell's equations) and the same solver techniques such as finite elements and finite-difference time domain, but components such as lasers, waveguides and ring modulators have no direct equivalent in the electrical domain, forcing deep specialization rather than an organic tool extension.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Explains why EDA majors are buying and building photonic specialists instead of extending existing SPICE-class tools — the capability gap is not incremental.
insights.quote: But at a component level, while you might deal with components such as a laser, you don’t have a direct equivalent of that in the electrical domain.
insights.locator: Niels Fache, Keysight EDA — 'From a physics perspective'

insights.claim: In most photonic designs every waveguide sits on the same GDS or OASIS layer, making it difficult for LVS to distinguish a waveguide acting as a wire from one acting as an active device that generates or modifies a signal.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A concrete, unsolved tool gap — sign-off vendors that fix layer/device disambiguation get a defensible photonic sign-off position.
insights.quote: These designs rely on waveguides, and in most designs, every waveguide is on the same GDS or OASIS layer, which makes it difficult to distinguish.
insights.locator: John Ferguson, Siemens EDA — 'From a verification perspective'

insights.claim: Because photons pass through one another largely unimpacted, photonic layouts contain waveguide crossings that verification tools must be taught not to flag as short circuits.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Signals that legacy sign-off decks generate large volumes of false errors on photonic layouts — a real productivity tax on early co-packaged optics programs.
insights.quote: Here the challenge is how to recognize that these crossings do not actually represent a short-circuit.
insights.locator: John Ferguson, Siemens EDA

insights.claim: Sign-off formats like GDSII and OASIS rasterize curves to grid points, so DRC tools see a distorted version of a photonic curve and report many false width and spacing violations that the design team must manually triage.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Creates demand for new curve-aware layout formats or de-rasterization waiver tooling — a discrete new product category inside physical verification.
insights.quote: In other words, the DRC tools do not see the curve as intended
insights.locator: John Ferguson, Siemens EDA — 'For DRC, the issue is'

insights.claim: Photonic design does not benefit from shrink, so photonic chips are often quite large, although they contain fewer total elements than a traditional design with little need for vias and stacked metals.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Photonics consumes wafer area per function without Moore's Law relief — die-cost curves and foundry capacity planning for PICs look nothing like logic.
insights.quote: Unlike the traditional IC environment, photonic design does rely on active elements, and as such does not benefit from shrinkage
insights.locator: John Ferguson, Siemens EDA — 'And because the waveguides are in silicon'

insights.claim: Photonic EDA work today is largely building glue between tools that were never designed to talk to each other: Lumerical FDTD for component physics, compact models feeding a circuit simulator like INTERCONNECT, layout in a cockpit like OptoDesigner, and thermal analysis running alongside optical simulation from early floor-planning.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Names the actual incumbent tool chain and the integration gap — the acquisition and consolidation target list for EDA majors moving into photonics.
insights.quote: Much of the ‘photonic EDA work’ is building the glue
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'What often happens is that engineering teams stitch together tools'

insights.claim: Photonics has no equivalent of digital formal verification: verifying a photonic design means simulating a handful of operating points, which is validation rather than proof.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: The verification hole is the single largest technical risk in scaling co-packaged optics — and the clearest whitespace for a new tool franchise.
insights.quote: Photonics has nothing equivalent; verification means simulating a handful of operating points, which is validation, not proof.
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'Where the flow remains immature'

insights.claim: Closing the photonic verification gap is described as the biggest opportunity in photonic tooling over the next five years.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A five-year window flagged by a formal-verification CEO — watch for EDA majors and startups targeting photonic functional verification specifically.
insights.quote: Closing that gap is the biggest opportunity in photonic tooling over the next five years.
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise

insights.claim: Formal rigor can be applied today not to the optics but to the digital logic surrounding it — the calibration state machines and tuning loops in the electronic IC — because a misbehaving tuning loop breaks an optical link just as surely as bad optics.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A near-term, sellable wedge for formal vendors into photonics programs without waiting for photonic formal methods to exist.
insights.quote: because a misbehaving tuning loop breaks a link just as surely as bad optics
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'Design-space exploration still happens with scripted sweeps'

insights.claim: Photonic design-space exploration still relies on scripted sweeps across wavelength, temperature and process corners — the same position digital verification occupied before formal methods existed.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A historical analogy that dates the maturity of photonic EDA: it is pre-formal, implying a decade of tool spend ahead.
insights.quote: Simulate what you can think of and hope the bug isn’t in the case you didn’t.
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise

insights.claim: For co-packaged optics the open question is no longer whether the photonic circuit works, but whether the assembled full electro-optical system — photonic chip, electronics chip, packaging, cooling and power delivery — behaves predictably at scale.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Reframes the risk in CPO deployments from device yield to system integration, which is where schedule slips in AI networking will originate.
insights.quote: So for co-packaged optics, the question is no longer about whether the photonic circuit works.
insights.locator: Raha Vafaei, Synopsys

insights.claim: Uncompensated silicon ring resonators drift roughly 70 to 80 picometers per degree Celsius, so a photonic design that is correct at room temperature can fail under self-heating.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A hard number quantifying why thermal control loops and heaters are mandatory content in every optical engine — a recurring BOM and power cost in CPO.
insights.quote: uncompensated silicon ring resonators drift roughly 70 to 80 picometers per degree Celsius, and a design correct at room temperature can fail under self-heating
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'Thermal analysis runs alongside optical simulation'

insights.claim: A degree of temperature drift can shift a ring modulator's resonance out of its WDM slot — a NAND gate stays a NAND gate when the room warms, but a ring can functionally break.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Explains why photonic reliability cannot be certified with digital-style margining, raising qualification cost and time for optical interconnect suppliers.
insights.quote: A NAND gate stays a NAND gate when the room warms, but a ring can functionally break.
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'Digital design controls a two-level system'

insights.claim: Silicon is indirect-bandgap and has no efficient native light source, so practically every silicon photonics system relies on an external or hybrid-bonded III-V laser.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Structural dependency: III-V/InP laser supply and hybrid-bonding capacity are a hard constraint on how fast co-packaged optics can scale.
insights.quote: silicon, being indirect-bandgap, has no efficient native light source, so practically every system relies on an external or hybrid-bonded III-V laser
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise

insights.claim: Digital design abstracts physics away so logic can be verified, but photonic design cannot, because in photonics the physics is the logic.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A compact mental model for why photonic tool spend per design will stay structurally higher than digital — abstraction cannot amortize it away.
insights.quote: Photonic design can’t, because the physics is the logic.
insights.locator: Ashish Darbari, Axiomise — 'Put simply, digital design abstracts the physics away'

insights.claim: A standard SPICE simulator models only voltages and currents, whereas a photonic simulator must also represent wavelength, optical phase, polarization, propagation loss, reflections, interference, resonances and often bidirectional signal flow.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Concrete measure of the capability gap between reusable electrical EDA and what photonics actually needs — reuse is partial, not free.
insights.locator: John Bowers — 'Using existing electrical tools to design optical devices'

insights.claim: In photonics the waveguide is not merely a connection with parasitics like an electrical wire; its geometry and performance change the actual function of the device, not just its performance margins.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Undercuts the assumption that photonic layout can be automated with electrical routing engines — a barrier to the productivity gains investors assume.
insights.quote: It’s not just a connection; it’s part of the device.
insights.locator: Raha Vafaei, Synopsys — 'Still, while existing electrical design tools are very important'

themes.theme: Automation, agentic AI and vendor positioning

insights.claim: Photonic chips have historically been handcrafted the way RF designs were 20 years ago, and as photonic die size grows it is no longer realistic to assume every part of a photonic chip will be hand-designed — but core photonic placement and routing automation still barely exists.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Identifies the missing product category in photonic EDA; the vendor that ships credible photonic place-and-route captures a new tool line as PIC volumes scale.
insights.quote: It’s no longer realistic to assume that every bit of a photonic chip will be handcrafted with love, so automation comes in, and AI can help.
insights.locator: Gilles Lamant, Cadence — 'What’s next for photonics design'

insights.claim: Agentic AI platforms are expected to orchestrate the currently fragmented optical-I/O flow, with AI agents continuously generating, simulating, verifying, diagnosing and optimizing the complete optical-I/O system.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Photonics is a natural first commercial beachhead for agentic EDA because the flow is manual and fragmented — watch EDA vendors monetize agents here first.
insights.quote: In the future, we expect to see a more automated electronic-photonic design environment in which AI agents continuously generate, simulate, verify, diagnose, and optimize the complete optical-I/O system.
insights.locator: John Bowers — 'AI represents an important opportunity'

insights.claim: Cadence explicitly positions the photonic IC as one chiplet inside a larger system built on its existing electronic platform, contrasting itself with university spinouts, startups and PIC-only tools that try to expand outward from the photonic die.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: A stated competitive fault line in photonic EDA: platform incumbents versus PIC-native startups — determines who wins co-packaged optics design seats.
insights.quote: For us, a photonic design is not an end in itself. It’s part of the system
insights.locator: Gilles Lamant, Cadence

insights.claim: The most productive photonic flow is not forcing photonic tools into electrical tools but connecting them so customers do not have to choose between photonic accuracy and EDA efficiency.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Frames Synopsys's product strategy — integration, not replacement — and the benchmark against which competing photonic flows will be sold.
insights.quote: the customers won’t have to choose between the accuracy of the photonics and the efficiency of the EDA
insights.locator: Raha Vafaei, Synopsys

insights.claim: As optical moves from a discrete component to a die inside the package, the system question shifts from 'Does the I/O work?' to 'How does data move coherently across optical and electrical domains?', and that integration layer is where the next hard problems sit.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: Points to system-integration IP (fabrics, NoCs) as an under-appreciated beneficiary of the shift to in-package optics.
insights.quote: As optical moves from a discrete component to a die inside the package, the center of gravity shifts from, ‘Does the I/O work?’ to ‘How does data move coherently across optical and electrical domains?’
insights.locator: Kent Orthner, Baya Systems

insights.claim: Photonics design remains a split flow in which specialized photonic tools handle electromagnetic simulation, waveguide layout and S-parameter extraction, then hand off to electrical and system simulation for the surrounding electronics.
insights.speaker: Ann Mutschler
insights.so_what: The handoff seam is where errors and schedule risk concentrate today — and the target for any vendor promising a unified electro-optical flow.
insights.locator: Kent Orthner, Baya Systems — 'From the perspective of how die-to-die optics affect'
